title: ProjectMemoryState
description: Canonical structure for a project's persisted MEMORY.md state. Validated in-memory before every Phase 4 Persistence Handshake write, whether rendered to Markdown or synced to an MCP memory graph.

tier3_domain_rules.description: Tier 3 — non-negotiable domain rules and user preferences. Append-and-supersede only; never garbage-collected by volume pressure.

tier2_architecture_log.description: Tier 2 — architecture decisions and long-term constraints, recorded as ADRs.

supersedes.description: The ADR id this entry replaces, if any.

superseded_by.description: Back-reference set on the OLD entry when a newer ADR supersedes it — the structured, queryable counterpart to `supersedes`, set on both sides of the link in the same write. Null while status is active.

source.description: Provenance: what conversation/session produced this decision, e.g. '2026-08-08 — tunnel auth discussion'. Free text, not a structured ID Claude doesn't reliably have access to.

last_referenced.description: Most recent date this entry was actually cited or relied upon again in a later session. Drives usage-based retention in consolidate-memory.md — an entry that keeps getting referenced ages out slower than the flat 7-day timer alone would allow. Null if never referenced since it was written.

tier1_active_tasks.description: Tier 1 — active execution state. High-volatility; heavily pruned each consolidation pass.

source.description: Provenance: what conversation/session produced this task.

compressed_changelog.description: Rolling archive of collapsed Tier 1/Tier 2 history — 2-line-per-window summaries produced by workflows/consolidate-memory.md.
